setup: uvicorn app.server:app (one process) on the real service and HydraDB release build, baton end-state graph (3,533 nodes, 24,491 links); 18 users on /route (test issues), 2 on /learn (reserve-pool issues, newest first), 60 s, MacBook, 12 cores
learning_writes: 51 /learn calls: 28 were real learning steps (issues_learned 1700 to 1728), the other 23 were reserve issues already in the graph as gap-filled history, which the service treats as a no-op

single_route_profile_ms.note: one route at a time, 300 test issues, no load

diagnosis: almost all route time is inside HydraDB's algo.MSpaths (about 250 ms with only pathWeight returned vs 256 ms with full paths); the node runs about 3.6 fresh path queries per second on one connection and about 8 to 9 per second at 8 in parallel, so 18 routing users queue at about 10 routes per second; no cheap change keeps routing results identical (maxLen 2, a smaller pathCount, history pruning or the graph-indexer would)
graph_after: restored with uv run python -m eval.restore_graph to the 1,700-issue snapshot: counts equal and all 300 test routes identical to before the run (top-1 0.670, top-3 0.823)
